claims.head: Top line on top line: Matthews vs. Benson
claims.call: The Maple Leafs’ L1 (Roslovic, Matthews and Marchenko) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sabres’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Maple Leafs keep sending Matthews’s line (Roslovic, Matthews and Marchenko) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Hiller has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Östlund and Quinn.

claims.head: There’s no curse: Luukkonen vs. The Maple Leafs
claims.body: Luukkonen has been shaky against the Maple Leafs since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
claims.nums: 6 starts against Toronto: .851 save percentage · .902 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Luukkonen’s record against the Maple Leafs.
claims.call: If Luukkonen starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .902 than to his .851 against the Maple Leafs.

TOR.head: Not an easy night for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage, Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

items.text: Auston Matthews has a point in ten straight games against Buffalo, and 15 points in his last ten against them.

The Sabres are newly without Rasmus Dahlin, and have had to make do without Alex Lyon all season. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is expected to start. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, only the Wild are missing more right now.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Chris Tanev.
Morgan Rielly is two goals from 100.
